metadata.title: Analysis and Figure-Reproduction Code for Loop Current-Yucatan Channel Covariability from Altimetry and Canek Mooring Observations
metadata.description:
Main covariability patterns between the Loop Current and the flow through the Yucatan Channel from altimetry and sustained moored observations

This archive contains MATLAB scripts and compact processed data used to reproduce the analyses and figures associated with the manuscript.

The study combines satellite-altimetry-derived surface circulation fields with sustained Canek velocity observations across the Yucatan Channel and Florida Straits. The analysis examines how the position, strength, and cross-sectional structure of the boundary currents covary with the extension, retraction, pathway, and eddy-detachment behavior of the Loop Current.

The maximum covariance analysis is based on the common Canek–altimetry period from 2011 to 2023. The identified Loop Current spatial modes are additionally projected over the longer 1993–2025 altimetric record for event and detachment diagnostics.

This archive contains compact, figure-ready processed products rather than the complete daily Canek and Copernicus Marine Service source datasets. The included files preserve the numerical fields, time series, event selections, diagnostics, and intermediate products required to reproduce the archived manuscript figures without redistributing the complete observational records.

ANALYSES INCLUDED

• Maximum covariance analysis between Yucatan Channel velocity observations and Loop Current geostrophic speed

• Independent EOF analysis of the Loop Current and Yucatan Channel fields

• Reconstruction and interpretation of the leading coupled modes

• Positive- and negative-phase composite analysis

• Time-normalized evolution of second-mode events

• Lagged correlations involving Yucatan Current core position and transport

• Partial least-squares reconstruction of the Loop Current surface state from the Yucatan and Florida Canek sections

• Independent identification of northwestern Caribbean anticyclones

• Objective identification of Loop Current detachments

• Matching of Loop Current detachments to preceding Mode-2 extrema

• Generation of the manuscript and Supporting Information figures represented in the archive

REPOSITORY CONTENTS

plotting/
Self-contained MATLAB routines for reproducing the archived figures.

data/
Compact MAT files containing the processed variables consumed by the plotting routines.

analysis/
Scripts documenting how selected processed products were calculated or extracted from the complete local analysis archive.

figures/
Reproduced PNG versions of the manuscript and Supporting Information figures included in the archive.

data/DATA_DICTIONARY.md
Descriptions of processed variables, units, spatial grids, sign conventions, and time conventions.

make_all_figures.m
Master MATLAB routine for reproducing the included figures.

MANIFEST.sha256
SHA-256 checksums for archive verification.

CITATION.cff
Machine-readable citation metadata.

README.md
Detailed repository description, requirements, and reproduction instructions.

The repository contains the materials required to reproduce manuscript Figures 2–10 and Supporting Information Figures S4–S5.

PROCESSED DATA INCLUDED

The processed files include:

• Maximum covariance spatial patterns and temporal coefficients

• Extended Loop Current modal coefficients projected over the altimetric record

• Surface and cross-sectional composite fields

• Yucatan Current core-position and transport diagnostics

• Loop Current area and detached-eddy area time series

• Lagged pointwise and multiple-correlation maps

• Testing-skill maps and selected fields from the diagnostic reconstruction

• Time-normalized event composites

• Curated Mode-2 event selections

• Objectively detected Loop Current detachment events

• Detachment locations and event-to-detachment lags

• Conditional composites based on preceding Mode-2 extrema

Large working files excluded from this archive include the complete daily Canek velocity matrices, full CMEMS/AVISO time series, complete regression-coefficient matrices, and other large intermediate analysis products.

REPRODUCING THE FIGURES

The plotting workflow was developed and tested using MATLAB R2023b.

To reproduce the included figures:

  1. Download the complete archive and preserve its directory structure.
  2. Start MATLAB in the repository root directory.
  3. Run:

make_all_figures

The reproduced PNG files will be written to the figures/ directory.

The public plotting routines use MATLAB built-in functionality together with the processed data included in this archive. They do not require the private coastline files or plotting utilities used during preparation of the original manuscript figures.

RELATED OBSERVATIONAL DATA

Canek mooring observations

The complete Canek Version 4 daily gridded velocity products for the Yucatan Channel and Florida Straits are distributed separately through Zenodo.

Canek Version 4 dataset:
https://zenodo.org/records/17887342

Satellite altimetry

Satellite absolute dynamic topography and geostrophic velocity fields were obtained from the Copernicus Marine Service:

Global Ocean Gridded L4 Sea Surface Heights and Derived Variables Reprocessed 1993 Ongoing

Product ID: SEALEVEL_GLO_PHY_L4_MY_008_047

DOI: https://doi.org/10.48670/moi-00148

The original Copernicus Marine Service data are not redistributed in this archive and remain subject to their original terms of access and use.

SCOPE OF REPRODUCIBILITY

The processed products included in this archive are sufficient to reproduce the archived figures and the numerical diagnostics represented by those figures.

Recalculation of every analysis directly from the original observations requires the separately archived Canek Version 4 velocity products, the corresponding Copernicus Marine Service altimetry products, and the analysis scripts included in this archive.

This record is therefore intended as a compact reproducibility package rather than as a redistribution of the complete observational datasets.

ASSOCIATED MANUSCRIPT

Durante, G., Sheinbaum, J., Larrañaga, M., Pallàs-Sanz, E., Send, U., Pérez-Brunius, P., Verdugo-Ortega, H., Zhang, Y., & Tanahara, S.

Main covariability patterns between the Loop Current and the flow through the Yucatan Channel from altimetry and sustained moored observations.

Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans.

Manuscript DOI:
[Insert DOI when available]

CITATION

Users of these materials should cite the associated manuscript, this Zenodo reproducibility archive, and the Canek Version 4 dataset when using the underlying Canek observational products.

The preferred citation for this repository is provided in CITATION.cff
